- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct; apply downward bias of 3–8% for 3–7 days post-spike.
- If sentiment shifts from neutral to positive (e.g., 0.00 → 0.67), model overreacts; dampen forecast by 1–3% for next 2–4 days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price is falling, model often underestimates drop; increase forecast downward bias by 2–5% for 3–5 days.
- Mean reversion bias: if price has been trending upward for 5+ days, model often fails to revert; apply downward correction of 1–4% for next 3–7 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate early in the forecast window; reduce first 5–7 days by 1–3% if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.7) and price is falling, model often fails to recognize trend reversal; apply upward bias of 1–3% for next 2–5 days.
